The basis of Republican attacks on Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul
El-Sayed for being "linked" to the Muslim Brotherhood is that his half-sister
said his mother, Fatten Elkomy, was active with the group in Egypt in the
1970s. El-Sayed was born in Rochester Hills, Michigan, in 1984. When he was
three, his parents divorced. He was raised by his father, Mohammed El-Sayed,
and stepmother, Jacqueline Johnson. In 2025, President Donald Trump
[designated](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-
actions/2025/11/designation-of-certain-muslim-brotherhood-chapters-as-foreign-
terrorist-organizations-and-specially-designated-global-terrorists/) some
chapters of the Muslim Brotherhood as terrorist organizations.

Ludicrous though the situation may be, El-Sayed has been forced to repeatedly
deny ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, including in an interview with NBC last
week.

**" I have no ties. We have no ties,"** he [told host Tom
Llamas](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/15/el-sayed-again-
denies-ties-muslim-brotherhood/). **" I have never had these conversations
with my mother. I wasn't raised by my mother ... You're using hearsay evidence
from a tweet. It's just not serious."**

It isn't, but of course such attacks persist. On Saturday, at a town hall in
Caro, Michigan, a young man who identified himself as Tommy stood to ask El-
Sayed:** "Will you disavow the Muslim Brotherhood?"**

El-Sayed said, **" Sure, yeah, absolutely,"** then asked: **" Why are you
asking the question?"**

The ensuing exchange, in which El-Sayed outlined the U.S. Constitution's
protections of all faiths and none, and charged his Christian questioner with
suggesting El-Sayed, a Muslim, has **" dual loyalties,"** ended with El-Sayed
drawing applause and Tommy leaving the room.

As the exchange went viral - helped, of course, by El-Sayed's campaign,
recognizing a clear win when it saw one - facts about Tommy came rushing out.
